english.title: Misuse profits of fund-raising lottery - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used part of the profits of a lottery for a purpose other than the fund-raising purpose stated by the promoter for the promotion of the lottery
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 260 and 263(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
used any part of the profits of a lottery
for a purpose other than the fund-raising purpose
stated by the promoter for the promotion of the lottery

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 260(3) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that "using profits" includes permitting profits to be used.
(ii)Section 260(4) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that the reference to a statement of a purpose for the promotion of a lottery is a reference to a statement appearing on lottery tickets or in an advertisement for the lottery.
(iii) Section 260(5) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that "advertisement" in relation to a lottery includes any written notice announcing that a lottery will take place or inviting people to participate in a lottery (in either case whether or not it also gives other information).
(iv) For the territorial application of this offence see section 265 of the Gambling Act 2005.
(v) A licensing authority may institute criminal proceedings in respect of this offence, section 346(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
